response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cu.customer_id, cu.gender, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Customers cu JOIN Orders o ON o.customer_id = cu.customer_id WHERE cu.gender IS NOT NULL GROUP BY cu.customer_id, cu.gender), s AS (SELECT customer_id, gender, n, n * 1.0 / SUM(n) OVER (PARTITION BY gender) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT s.*, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT customer_id, gender, n AS order_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_above_average FROM a WHERE share > avg_share ORDER BY share_above_average DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The average share is the simple average of the per-customer shares across all customers who have orders and a non-NULL gender, with all genders pooled. It is not computed per gender.
'No gender recorded' means gender IS NULL. Empty-string genders are treated as recorded values.
Shares are computed as decimal (non-integer) values and are not rounded.
